articles.title: Third person arrested in death of Tasia Fortune, as police say hanging was staged
articles.summary: Eric Clark, 45, charged with murder as autopsy concludes Fortune was dead days before body discovered in tree A third person has been arrested in the death of 29-year-old Tasia Fortune in Mississippi…

blocks.text: A third person has been arrested in the death of 29-year-old Tasia Fortune in Mississippi’s capital city, while investigators said they had determined the scene where her body was found hanging had been staged.
Eric Clark, 45, surrendered to authorities on Friday and was charged with murder, according to the Jackson police department (JPD). Clark was scheduled to make a court appearance on Monday.
Police disclosed Friday that an autopsy investigation concluded “the scene and the hanging were staged”.
Authorities did not release additional information about the circumstances surrounding Fortune’s killing or why investigators believe the scene was faked.
Clark’s arrest comes after two other men, Earnest Lloyd Jr and Jarques Ratliff, were charged with murder in connection with Fortune’s death.
The case leading to the arrests of Clark, Lloyd Jr and Ratliff had drawn national attention because of the severity of Fortune’s killing and Mississippi’s history of racist violence and lynchings.
Clark, Lloyd Jr, Ratliff are Black, as was Fortune.

“The Jackson police department’s robbery-homicide division will continue its investigation until all individuals believed to be involved are held accountable for their actions in connection with Ms Fortune’s death,” a news release shared with multiple news outlets states.
Fortune, a mother of four, was discovered on 3 August hanging from a tree behind a vacant home on the 500 block of Road of Remembrance in the western part of Jackson.
Investigators have said Fortune was not killed at the location where her body was found.

JPD detective Samuel Dukes previously described Fortune’s hanging in court as “staged”, saying investigators believe she was killed somewhere else before her body was placed in a hanging position in the tree on Road of Remembrance. He added investigators determined Fortune had been dead for two to three days before her body was discovered.
Police have released few details about the events leading to Fortune’s death. Detectives have interviewed as many as 15 people, according to the police news release.

Local TV news station WLBT reported an alleged physical altercation between Lloyd, 25, and Fortune that occurred shortly before her death. Police accused Lloyd of using a black cable cord to hang Fortune, according to WLBT.
Ratliff and Lloyd have both reportedly pleaded not guilty. Each has been denied bond.
Fortune’s mother, Christy Spivey, has said she was certain her daughter would not have killed herself.

articles.title: Palace tells Sara Duterte: Defend with proof, not fallacies
articles.summary: Malacañang hit back at Vice President Sara Duterte on Saturday, telling her to learn to recognize the flaws and fallacies in her arguments after she accused the Marcos administration of being…

blocks.text: Published September 27, 2026 1:15am

Malacañang hit back at Vice President Sara Duterte on Saturday, telling her to recognize the flaws and fallacies in her arguments after she accused the Marcos administration of being “desperate” to bring her down.

In a Viber message to reporters, Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro urged Duterte to address the accusations against her with evidence rather than relying on fallacies in defending herself.
“Maturuan sana ang Bise Presidente na matuto siyang sumagot nang may ebidensiya sa mga inaakusa sa kanya bago magturo ng iba,” Castro said in a Viber message to reporters.
(May the Vice President learn to answer the accusations against her with evidence before pointing fingers at others.)

Castro was responding to Duterte's accusation, which she made while denying allegations that she knew and received money from Rodolfo Gracioso Jr., a former policeman who served as a security officer for then-House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.
The Vice President dismissed the claims as another media stunt and a desperate move by the administration to bring her down and breathe life into the “faltering impeachment case” against her.
“The desperation of the administration to bring me down, push for Charter Change, prevent the 2028 elections, and cling to power is becoming increasingly diabolical,” Duterte said.
Castro said Duterte should familiarize herself with logical fallacies and improve how she responds to the allegations.
“Alamin niya ang definition ng red herring at ad hominem fallacies para malaman niya ang kamalian niya sa pakikipag-argumento,” she said.
(May she learn the definition of red herring and ad hominem fallacies so she can understand the flaws in her arguments.)

“Uulit-ulitin natin para tumimo sa isipan (We will repeat this again and again so it sticks in her mind): She needs to level up her defending skills so she can appear credible, if only for once,” she added.

In an exclusive interview with GMA News, Gracioso alleged that he delivered suitcases containing cash to Duterte, former President Rodrigo Duterte, and Davao City 1st District Representative Paolo Duterte on Velasco's instructions.
Gracioso estimated that he had delivered a total of more than P2 billion to the Vice President.
For his part, Velasco also denied the allegations against him, asserting that they were completely baseless.

“The former Speaker of the House's record of service in the government is untainted with corruption and his wife's benevolence is widely known, leaving no basis for the illegal allegations now being suggested,” said Velasco's spokesperson, Atty. Rowell Ilagan, in a statement.
The National Bureau of Investigation said it has begun its probe into Gracioso's claims. — MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Wisconsin police investigating fraternity for hazing after men found in basement
articles.summary: Pledges found covered in food in heated basement of fraternity house near University of Wisconsin-Madison Police are investigating suspected illegal hazing after about 30 partially clothed young men…

blocks.text: Police are investigating suspected illegal hazing after about 30 partially clothed young men covered in food, condiments and other liquids were found recently in the basement of a fraternity house near the University of Wisconsin-Madison campus.
Madison police said some of the men, whom they described as pledges of a fraternity, had signs of being physically assaulted.

Police went to the Alpha Epsilon Pi (AEPi) fraternity house on Wednesday night after receiving an anonymous tip. Two fraternity members, both 20, were arrested on tentative misdemeanor charges of hazing and disorderly conduct, police said. No formal charges had been filed against them as of Friday morning.
The university said it was taking the case seriously and launching its own investigation.
“UW–Madison is fully committed to preventing and addressing hazing and takes all incidents involving our community seriously,” the university said in a Thursday statement.
Any student found to have broken the law or university policy could be subject to sanctions ranging from a written reprimand to expulsion, UW-Madison said.

Police released a photo that shows about two dozen men, all shirtless, in the basement of the fraternity with trash and other debris on the ground. The faces of the people in the photo are blurred out.

Police said the thermostat had been set to 81F, causing hot and humid conditions in the basement, where the walls appeared to be painted black. A majority of people in the basement were 18 years old, police said.

The fraternity’s status as a recognized student organization on the Madison campus was terminated in 2015 for holding events while suspended. It had been suspended in 2013 for hosting a party in which a 17-year-old and another person were taken to detox after being served alcohol at a party hosted by the fraternity, according to university records.
The termination came after a fourth incident involving either events, alcohol or both, the university said.
Since 2016, there were seven additional allegations involving the fraternity related to intramural sports, disrespectful behavior, drinking and hazing, the university said.
Because the fraternity is still recognized by its national organization, it is able to operate as a fraternity chapter unaffiliated with the university, UW-Madison said.

National fraternity spokesperson Jon Pierce said his organization is taking the allegations “very seriously” and will cooperate fully with investigations. Any member found to have participated will be expelled from the fraternity, he said.
“Hazing is a betrayal of everything our fraternity stands for,” Pierce said. “There is no place for it in AEPi. No exceptions. No excuses.”
The fraternity house is located just blocks from the heart of the UW-Madison campus, which is home to about 52,000 students.

Police said their investigation is also ongoing. The university’s office of student conduct and community standards is also investigating in accordance with its nonacademic misconduct process, UW-Madison said.

articles.title: Greek authorities seek answers after six killed in Athens apartment block explosion
articles.summary:
Emergency teams discovered victims after two-storey building in historic Plaka district collapsed ‘in a matter of seconds’

Greek authorities say they are trying to discover what caused a…

blocks.text: Greek authorities say they are trying to discover what caused a two-storey apartment block in the heart of ancient Athens to collapse “in a matter of seconds”, killing six people.
Emergency teams found the victims, including four American tourists, on Saturday, more than 24 hours after an explosion prompted the early morning tragedy in the historic Plaka district.

The fire service said the bodies of three women and three men had been found, but stopped short of identifying them. A Briton and his Greek wife, aged 77 and 78, who lived in a flat on the building’s upper floor, were among those killed, the Guardian was told.

“The bodies have been taken to the morgue where postmortems will be conducted,” the city’s vice-mayor Paris Charlaftis said in a telephone interview from the blast scene. “Our focus now is on the explosion’s cause. What could have happened to bring the building down in a matter of seconds?”

Rescuers had deployed thermal cameras and geophones, used to detect deep subsonic frequencies, in the hope of finding survivors. Earth-moving machines and specially trained search dogs were brought in to move and comb mounds of rubble through the night.

Before the bodies were pulled from the ruins on Saturday, police put the missing at six, saying four were Americans staying in a short-term rental on the building’s first floor. Two brothers and their wives, all four were due to fly to the US on Friday, just hours after the explosion.

blocks.caption: Police have put the missing at six. Photograph: Costas Baltas/Anadolu/Getty Images

blocks.text: “When they failed to turn up for the flight they had checked into only a day earlier, that gave us a further lead,” a source said. “It became clearer that they must have been there when the blast occurred.”

The Briton, a talented artist, who lived with his wife on the second floor, was described as being partially disabled by Charlaftis. “He had kinetic issues, and it was thought likely they, too, were in the building [at the time of the blast].”

Nestled around the foot of the fifth-century BC Acropolis, Plaka is especially popular with tourists. The picturesque district draws thousands of visitors daily, with many staying overnight in the hotels and short-term rentals in neoclassical houses and small apartment blocks along its alleyways and narrow streets.
The mayor of Athens, Haris Doukas, who rushed to 15 Lysikratous where the mid-20th century building had once stood, was quick to describe the incident as an “unprecedented disaster”.

At least three people were known to have been injured when the 7.30am explosion occurred, shattering the windows of nearby buildings and scattering debris far and wide. A motorist driving down Lysikratous described how his car was lifted into the air by the sheer force of a blast that some in the neighbourhood likened to an earthquake, others to a bomb. Emergency workers could be seen hastily removing two women on stretchers from a building next door who had been wounded by flying debris.

Speculation is rife that a gas leak triggered the collapse but officials said there were many “cogent theories” at play. Fears of the leak emanating from the first-floor short-term rental was among them.
after newsletter promotion
As part of efforts to address a burgeoning housing crisis, Greece’s centre-right government has sought to ban short-term rentals in Plaka – clamping down on permits and tightening regulations.
On Saturday, as speculation mounted over the cause of the blast, criticism grew over the ability to “properly control” establishments that were often unregulated.

“This awful incident will fuel further debate over who inspects short-term rentals that no one who lives in Plaka wants anyway,” said Giorgos Zafeiriou, an architect who heads the local residents’ committee. “Hotels have chambers that regulate them but who inspects and controls Airbnb and serviced apartments that often may not be up to par?”
Civil protection crews and emergency disaster management teams have been ordered to remain on site until the cause of the explosion is found, officials said.
“It was a huge explosion, so getting to the bottom of it must now be the priority,” added Zafeiriou. “Six people have lost their lives.”

articles.title: China, US agree to set up channel for AI safety incidents
articles.summary: Following the summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, the two superpowers pledged to set up a "communication channel" for AI incidents and boost coordination on…

image.caption: The two leaders are expected to meet twice more before the end of the yearImage: Jim Watson/AFP

blocks.text: Beijing and Washington promised to expand dialogue on AI safety and between the countries' militaries while also cutting tariffs on about $30 billion (€26.3 billion) of "non-sensitive goods."
The pledges follow the three-day summit between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in the US.
US President Trump described the summit in an online post as "one of Friendship, Strength, and Success" for both nations.
Trump-Xi summit: Results or just symbolism?
China's President Xi was more constrained, saying the two sides agree on "strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness, and reciprocity."
Beijing and Washington to improve military communication

On Saturday, with Xi back in Beijing, China said the two sides agreed to a mutual tariff reduction on roughly $30 billion of "non-essential" goods. This applies to exports such as agricultural products or holiday decorations.
The Chinese statement also confirmed that the two side will be setting up a "communication channel" for AI incidents.

"Artificial intelligence technologies are continuously developing, all parties can strengthen exchanges, discuss in-depth and seek consensus in light of the latest situation," the Chinese Foreign Ministry said.
A new round of AI-focused dialogue is due to be held in November.
The two nations will also accelerate their work on military crisis communications, Beijing said, without providing details.
Xi to travel to the US again in December

The US had previously announced that Beijing and Washington agreed to extend their "trade truce" agreed by Trump and Xi in Busan last October. The agreement, which saw China suspending its controls on rare earths and the US cutting back on some of its tariffs, was due to expire on November 10. According to US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, the deal will remain in effect until January.
Trump hosts China's Xi for state visit

The White House also said the two sides addressed American concerns about rare earths supply "with the goal of ensuring shipment levels return to appropriate levels." China also agreed to import at least 10 million metric tons of coal from the US in 2027 and 2028, according to the Trump administration.

While Donald Trump confirmed the Iran war was also on the agenda during the US talks, no major breakthroughs were reported on the issue. However, the Chinese Foreign Ministry said both sides agreed that Iran should not have nuclear weapons, and no country should impose transit tolls on international waterways, in reference to the Strait of Hormuz.

Trump and Xi are due to meet twice more by the end of the year, with Trump expected to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation ​summit in China in November and Xi expected back in the US for a G20 summit in December, which is due to be hosted in Trump's National Doral Miami golf club.

articles.title: US strikes on Ecuadorian fishing boats raise humanitarian concerns but Trump admin not wavering
articles.summary:
Attorney says fishers ‘losing their livelihoods’, but Marco Rubio maintains US still willing to ‘blow up ships if need be’

While the US secretary of state,

blocks.text: While the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, was being decorated in Quito by Ecuador’s president for “helping to promote peace in the region”, 10 Ecuadorian fishers whose boat had been blown up by US forces were adrift in the eastern Pacific.

blocks.caption: Ecuador’s president, Daniel Noboa, right, presents the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, with Ecuador’s highest ranking National Order of Merit, the Grand Cross, at Carondelet palace in Quito, on 9 September. Photograph: Dolores Ochoa/AP

blocks.text: On 8 September, a day before Rubio arrived, a US patrol vessel intercepted the fishing boat Don Rufo in international waters near Ecuador.

“The gringos were all armed as if they were going to war,” said the boat’s captain, Mero Calderón, 50. “I tried to show them our catch to prove that we were there working, but they wouldn’t listen,” he added.

blocks.caption: A US patrol vessel intercepting the fishing boat Don Rufo in international waters near Ecuador. Photograph: US Southern Command/X

blocks.text: “They brought two huge bombs aboard, took us to their ship, handcuffed and blindfolded us, and blew our boat to pieces,” said Calderón, who along with five other fishers, was handed over to local authorities.

But another 10 crew members were fishing farther out to sea in a smaller boat that was not equipped to make it back to shore. The Ecuadorian navy only rescued them on 10 September, when Rubio was already in Peru preparing to return to the US.

blocks.caption: Ten crew members from the five skiffs belonging to the vessel Don Rufo, after they were located and taken aboard the BAE Atahualpa, following air-maritime search and reconnaissance operations conducted by the Ecuadorian navy. Photograph: Ecuadorian Navy

blocks.text: US Southern Command posted an edited 14-second video of the operation and said “intelligence confirmed” that the vessel was being used by a gang as a “floating refuelling station” for speedboats allegedly carrying drugs – which the fishers deny.

It was one of eight operations involving Ecuadorian boats in just more than two weeks – the latest on 16 September – to follow the same pattern. Unlike the nearly 70 US airstrikes in the Pacific and Caribbean that have killed 234 people since last year, crews were removed before the vessels were sunk.

blocks.caption: A still from a video released by US forces intercepting a floating refuelling station supporting illicit at-sea drug trafficking operations in the eastern Pacific. Photograph: US Southern Command @Southcom

blocks.text: Also, rather than unilateral US attacks, the new wave of operations has the open support of Ecuador’s far-right president, Daniel Noboa, who is calling them “joint operations”.

Donald Trump has compared the drug trafficking operations to the campaign against the Islamic state. “Like ISIS, they should be killed, exiled or detained as enemy combatants without the possibility of release, which is what we’re doing,” Trump said on Tuesday.
Some analysts see the shift as an indication that the US’s military strategy against drug trafficking in Latin America has entered a new phase.

blocks.caption: Marines and sailors with Maritime Raid Force, LCF-24, boarding the Ecuadorian fishing vessel Conquista 2 in the Pacific on 2 September. Photograph: US Marine Corps Forces, South

blocks.text: “Noboa has offered Ecuador as a ‘laboratory’ for the implementation of this new phase,” said Will Freeman, a fellow for Latin America studies at the Council on Foreign Relations.

Although Ecuador does not produce cocaine like neighbouring Colombia and Peru, over the past decade it has become a major trafficking hub because of its access to the Pacific, including the area where the attacks on boats have been taking place.
Noboa has responded with a controversial “iron-fist” approach to the gangs, issuing repeated states of emergency and expanding the role of the armed forces.

blocks.caption: Relatives of the four minors apprehended by soldiers and found dead near a military base dance during a rally to demand justice a year after their apprehension in Guayaquil, Ecuador on 8 December 2025. Photograph: Marcos Pin/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: This crackdown however has done little to reduce violence, and instead has eroded human rights. The most notable example of human rights abuse came last year in the case of the “Guayaquil Four”, the forced disappearance of four Afro-Ecuadorian boys between the age of 11 and 15. All four boys were found dead, there bodies charred and dismembered.

Despite pushback from voters, Noboa signed an agreement with the White House authorising joint operations and granting US military personnel involved in counter-narcotics operations immunity from criminal prosecution. The operations have also extended to land, with US troops taking part in raids last Thursday.

“Noboa is interested in the optics of a very lethal crackdown and in making Ecuador a place where the Trump administration can refine those methods and show them off,” said Freeman, who has also reported on the boat attacks in Ecuador for the New Yorker magazine.

blocks.caption: People look at the remains of a burned-out fishing boat in the port of Manta, Ecuador, on 6 June 2026. The Ecuadorian national police said at least 20 fishing boats had been damaged.   Photograph: Ariel Ochoa/EPA
The Ecuadorean army shows drug trafficker Adolfo Macías, alias Fito, being guarded after his recapture in Manta, which is in the Manabi province. Photograph: Ecuadorean Army/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Trump has pressured Latin American presidents to join an anti-drug cartel coalition he created called Shield of the Americas. With Peru and Colombia recently joining, the group now includes all but the few countries still governed by the left, such as Mexico and Brazil – where a far-right senator is a serious contender in October’s election.
So far, the coalition’s primary goal appears to have been increasing joint operations against alleged drug traffickers.
Adam Isacson, director for defence oversight at the Washington Office on Latin America, expects joint operations to expand across the region.

blocks.caption: Fishermen work along the shore as local fishermen are increasingly being pursued by Ecuadorean gangs to move drugs and for their skills navigating the Pacific waters along Ecuador’s coast, in Manta, on 4 June. Photograph: Karen Toro/Reuters

blocks.text: Isacson stressed that though more people are being turned over to local authorities instead of killed, the US is “still doing the bad old stuff”. On 19 September, four people were killed in the Caribbean. As with the other airstrikes, the US has not disclosed their identities or any of the alleged evidence linking them to criminal activity.

During his trip to Ecuador, Rubio said the decision on what approach to take was “a strike-by-strike or operation-by-operation determination” that depended on the threat and location of the boat, but that the US would “still blow up ships if need be”.

Human rights organisations have described the airstrikes as extrajudicial killings, and a special rapporteur for the UN human rights council has concluded that there are “reasonable grounds to believe” that they constitute “crimes against humanity”.
Despite Trump’s claims, available data show they have had no impact on the volume of cocaine entering the country.

Journalists and human rights groups have managed to identify some of the victims, who in many cases were innocent or, when suspected of involvement in criminal activity, poor people at the bottom of trafficking networks.

blocks.caption: Relatives wait for 32 crew members to be released under precautionary measures in Manta, Ecuador, on 8 September 2026. The 24 crew members of the Maria Candelaria and eight from the Conquista II face judicial proceedings on suspicion of illicit association and fuel trafficking after their vessels…

blocks.text: In Ecuador, the local NGO Permanent Committee for the Defence of Human Rights estimates that more than 220 fishers have been subjected to “violent boardings, arbitrary detentions, enforced disappearances, torture and the destruction of vessels” in this year’s US operations.
None of the fishers remains in custody and, while some are still facing prosecution, many have already been acquitted for lack of evidence.

“Fishers are losing their livelihoods when the US destroys the boats. Besides, if the US says the vessels were being used to refuel drug boats, why destroy the evidence?” said the committee’s lawyer, Fernando Bastías.
A US Southern Command spokesperson said it conducts operations “in compliance with US and international law” and that leaving boats “intact could permit their reuse by criminal networks”.
Although the US and Ecuador have celebrated the recent operations on social media, three cases from earlier this year remain unclaimed.

The first was on 20 January, when the fishing vessel Fiorella disappeared with eight crew members on board; days earlier, some of them had told relatives they were being monitored by drones and by a vessel on which they said they had seen a US flag.

Human rights organisations and journalists identified two more cases with similar patterns in late March, although the fishers survived. The Washington Post reported that the three cases were part of a covert CIA programme, and the agency declined to comment.
A US Southern Command spokesperson said it had no knowledge of, nor were its forces “involved in the incidents described in reports involving the Fiorella”.

blocks.caption: Maria Mero and her mother, Maria Cueva, speak during an interview after Mero’s husband Gabriel Aladino Mero Delgado and brother Jefferson Ariel Mero Cueva disappeared from the boat Fiorella after a strike in June 2026. Photograph: Karen Toro/Reuters
Maria Cueva holding a picture of her son Jefferson Ariel Mero Cueva. Photograph: Karen Toro/Reuters

blocks.text: Both the husband and brother of María Mero, 43, were aboard the Fiorella: Gabriel Aladino Mero Delgado, 44, and Jefferson Ariel Mero Cueva, 25. “Where did they take them? Do they have them in the US, in a prison somewhere? We don’t want any trouble; we just want them to send them back to us,” she told the Guardian.
The families say they have spent months trying to get answers from the Ecuadorian government, so far without success.

“They were fishers, not criminals. Let the great president come here to my house and see whether I have luxuries, anything that would show I’m a drug trafficker. No, because all of us here are poor, and we just want our loved ones back,” added Mero.

articles.title: Trump rejects Iranian proposal to open Strait of Hormuz and end fighting
articles.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Saturday he had rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end fighting in the Middle East.

image.caption: U.S. President Donald Trump arrives to board Air Force One for travel to Tennessee from Joint Base Andrews, in Maryland on Saturday. Before leaving, Trump said he had rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. (Jonathan Ernst/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New
U.S. President Donald Trump said on Saturday he had rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end fighting in the Middle East.
A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Iran would show no ​flexibility over its nuclear program

Iran raised the initiative at the UN General Assembly in New York, saying it had been transmitted to the Americans via Qatari mediators and that it could reopen the strategic waterway and put an end to hostilities in the region within seven days.
But in comments to reporters at the White House, Trump said: "I reject their proposal.... I rejected their deal."
"They want to make a deal to open the Hormuz Strait immediately because they're losing so badly," he said before leaving for Tennessee. "We're winning tremendously."

"They want to make a deal and I think that's fine, I like making a deal, too. What they want to do is immediately open the Hormuz Strait ... because they have no money coming in, because they get their money from the Hormuz Strait," Trump said.

The U.S. has imposed an economic blockade on Iran to put pressure on Tehran to lift its blockade, which has drastically reduced shipping through the strait, even though Trump again asserted that the U.S. had control of the waterway.
The Wall Street Journal first reported that Trump had rejected the Iranian proposal, citing unnamed U.S. officials.
It said Trump was privately skeptical that Iran would meet his demands and had told his staff that he sees a renewed bombing campaign as likely after the November U.S. midterm elections.

items: What’s it like to smuggle sheep across the Strait of Hormuz? This film gives you a taste

blocks.text: A U.S. official had said earlier that discussions with Iran through mediators were "positive and constructive."
Conflict has disrupted oil flows, harmed global economy

The Iranians also engaged their Saudi rivals regarding the Strait of Hormuz, underscoring the stakes of a seven-month-old conflict that has disrupted oil flows through a critical shipping lane and taken a toll on the global economy.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told reporters at the United Nations on Friday the proposed deal would trigger a seven-day countdown to reopening the strait and a pause in regional fighting.

"If there is seriousness on the U.S. side to come to a deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, everything is now prepared," Araghchi said. If the U.S. were to agree, the warring parties could start wider talks "on mutually agreed subjects."
'We will not bow our head,' Iranian president says in UN General Assembly address

That could potentially include discussions of Iran's nuclear program. Trump has said Tehran must never acquire a nuclear bomb, while a senior Iranian official told Reuters that Iran would show no ​flexibility over its nuclear program even if the U.S. accepted its peace deal.
Iran would grant no concessions over its rights, including ​enriching uranium or shipping its ​highly enriched uranium out ⁠of the country, the official said.

items: Iran's president says country won't surrender after Trump threat to 'annihilate' Islamic republic

blocks.text: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, in an interview with the CBS show Face the Nation, said Tehran was ready for talks on its nuclear program and other issues but would not accept "bullying or coercion."
"Iran is not seeking war, but will defend itself against pressure, threats and attacks,” Pezeshkian said, adding that it had already agreed that "we're not supposed to develop nuclear weapons."
Previous attempts at diplomacy have failed to end the war, which began on Feb. 28 with U.S. and Israeli attacks.
Since then, the war has alternated between pauses and renewed strikes, killing thousands while degrading Iran's conventional forces and damaging Iran's already ailing economy.

Iran and its allies have retaliated by extending the conflict throughout the region. Iran has struck U.S. allies in the Gulf with drones and missiles while its Houthi allies in Yemen have targeted Saudi interests.

articles.summary: The Philippines has called for stronger cooperation on safe, orderly and stronger migration among member-countries of the United Nations.

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines has called for stronger cooperation on safe, orderly and stronger migration among member-countries of the United Nations.

“Migration is a Philippine reality,” Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro said yesterday, highlighting the scale of the Filipino diaspora and noting that many Filipinos abroad consider their host countries their “second homes.”
Lazaro made the remarks at a forum on “Forging Alliances: Strengthening Collaboration Along Migration Routes” held on the sidelines of the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly (UNGA) in New York.

“As a Champion country of the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly, and Regular Migration, the Philippines is committed to protecting, promoting and fulfilling the human rights of migrants throughout their migration journey,” she stressed.
While the Philippines has made significant progress in strengthening migration governance, Lazaro acknowledged that gaps persist.
“No country can address these challenges alone. This is why collective action, grounded in shared responsibility, is essential,” she said.

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Information and Communications Technology is investigating a potential data breach involving 48 companies participating in its trust assessment provider (DTAP) accredited program.
Among the files, which may have been exposed are corporate registration records, permits, certifications, cybersecurity credentials, employment documents and DICT performance evaluations.
An investigation has been launched to verify the reported exposure, including the authenticity, source, nature and extent of the data involved.

Should it be proven that personal or other protected data has been compromised, DICT “will take appropriate action,” including informing the affected companies in accordance with Republic Act 10173, or the Data Privacy Act, the DICT said. It assured accredited assessment providers that it is addressing the issue.
“DICT remains committed to the security of information entrusted to it and to the integrity of the DTAP accreditation program,” it said.

articles.title: Ombudsman urges NBI: Pursue Davao flood control probe
articles.summary: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla has called on the National Bureau of Investigation to pursue its investigation on alleged irregularities in government-funded infrastructure projects in Davao City.

blocks.text: September 27, 2026 | 12:00am
Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla
STAR / Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla has called on the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) to pursue its investigation on alleged irregularities in government-funded infrastructure projects in Davao City.
“I hope the NBI’s ongoing investigation in Davao continues,” Remulla said in the “Executive Session” program on dzRH yesterday.

According to earlier reports, the NBI is looking into allegations that a single contractor named Genesis 88 bagged around P7 billion worth of flood control projects implemented by the Department of Public Works and Highways in Davao City – previously labeled by the Ombudsman as the “epicenter” of anomalous flood control projects – from 2018 to 2024.
Six of the 51 flood control projects in the city flagged by the NBI could be considered “ghost” or nonexistent.

Remulla made the remark after one of the program’s hosts brought up the issue of the NBI examining the affidavit filed by former policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. stating that he had delivered suitcases containing P2 billion to Vice President Sara Duterte. Gracioso also claimed in his affidavit of having delivered cash in suitcases to the Vice President’s father, former president Rodrigo Duterte and to her brother, Davao City Rep. Paolo Duterte.

articles.title: Lacson calls for ‘fair’ verdict in Duterte trial
articles.summary: Sen. Panfilo Lacson has called for a “fair” and “evidence-based” verdict in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

blocks.text: September 27, 2026 | 12:00am
MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Panfilo Lacson has called for a “fair” and “evidence-based” verdict in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

Lacson made the remark during the Philippine Constitution Association’s 65th anniversary celebration in Makati yesterday when asked what kind of decision would help bring stability after a politically polarizing impeachment trial.

“A fair decision will bring stability to the country. As long as the decision is fair and based on evidence as presented without any political color, then it will bring stability to the country,” Lacson said.
He pointed out that the trial has yet to wrap up the prosecution’s presentation of evidence before the defense takes its turn.
“The defense has not yet presented their evidence. We only hear one side of the story. We need to hear the other side,” Lacson said.
The senator said fast-tracking the trial should mean maximizing the limited trial time without compromising evidence.
The Senate impeachment court will have a full week of proceedings this week, with whole-day trial dates set in the first half of October.
The verdict, which is expected to be heard by year-end, should be guided by the Constitution and by the weight of evidence, not by political considerations or public opinion, Lacson said.

In his speech, Lacson said accountability as enshrined in the 1987 Constitution is a tool to fight corruption and ensure honesty and integrity among public servants in the wake of the flood control mess.
He was referring to the Constitution’s provision that “Public office is a public trust,” which he said is a principle that cannot be compromised or negotiated.
Lacson threw shade at public officials who cry political persecution when investigated for malfeasance, instead of facing the allegations with confidence and conviction.
Constitutional crisis?

A law expert, meanwhile, has warned of a possible constitutional crisis amid the filing of petitions before the Supreme Court questioning the legality of the Senate impeachment court’s decision to lower the number of votes needed to convict the Vice President.

In an interview with dzMM, San Beda University-Manila Graduate School of Law Dean Rev. Fr. Ranhilio Aquino said the petitions filed by former executive secretary Vic Rodriguez and lawyer Ernesto Francisco Jr. were premature.
“The cases are premature because the decision of the Senate has not been used yet. It has not yet been applied on the respondent, Vice President Duterte,” Ranhilio said.

“To be able to bring a case in court, you should be the one affected in the decision of the Senate. Of course, they can use grounds like citizen suits, lawyer suits, and public interest suits. But basically, the rule is that you cannot file a case in the Supreme Court that you are not directly affected,” Ranhilio added. — Bella Cariaso

articles.title: Pope Leo celebrates open-air mass before 700,000 people in Paris
articles.summary:
Crowds line Place de la Concorde on second day of pontiff’s first official papal visit to France in 18 years

Hundreds of thousands of people lined the Avenue des Champs-Élysées in…

blocks.text: Hundreds of thousands of people lined the Avenue des Champs-Élysées in ⁠Paris on Saturday to attend an open-air mass with Pope Leo, on the second day of his visit to France.
The Vatican estimated 700,000 people turned out for the outdoor mass with the 71-year-old American pope – about 100,000 more than the number of people who had registered to attend.

It took place at the Place de la Concorde, the site of bloody executions by guillotine during the French Revolution – when Louis XVI’s staunchly Catholic rule was overthrown – and now the centre of the secular republic.
The choice of the site, a symbol of the French republic to many, was criticised by supporters of France’s strict legislation separating church and state in public life.

blocks.caption: Worshippers gather at the Place de la Concorde for Pope Leo’s open-air mass. Photograph: Stéphane Cardinale/Corbis/Getty Images

blocks.text: But cheers rang out in the crowd as the pope thanked ‌God in his homily for the chance to ‌visit France on a whirlwind four-day, three-city tour to promote Catholicism and its teachings.
It is the first official papal visit to France in 18 years.

Pope Leo asked those in the crowd not to keep their faith to themselves. “Let it overflow, so that those you meet may be refreshed and their thirst satisfied,” he said. “From this beautiful city of Paris, I pray fervently that the living water of the Holy Spirit may flow throughout France.”
He told Catholics that only their faith, and not material things, can provide true happiness.
“Only God can fill the emptiness within us,” he said.

blocks.caption: Pope Leo greets crowds lining the Champs-Élysées on the second day of his visit to France. Photograph: Kiran Ridley/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: The security zone for the event – the biggest of the papal tour – stretched about 1.4 miles (2.2km), shutting down road traffic in central Paris from the Place de la Concorde to the Arc de Triomphe and beyond.

Chanting “Leo, Leo” and “Long live the pope”, crowds of people waved French and Vatican flags as the pontiff rode slowly down the grand boulevard of the Champs-Élysées aboard a popemobile – a specially designed, partly open vehicle used during public appearances.

He stopped frequently along the way as babies were lifted out of the crowd and brought to him to receive a papal caress on their heads. The city centre was sealed off for the service, with helicopters circling overhead and snipers positioned on rooftops.

blocks.caption: Pope Leo delivered an outdoor mass to an estimated 700,000 people in Paris. Photograph: Stéphane Cardinale/Corbis/Getty Images

blocks.text: About 14,500 police officers, gendarmes, military personnel and firefighters were deployed to the event, which was attended by 2,400 priests and deacons, and about 100 bishops.
Marie-Élisabeth, a 44-year-old nun from Burgundy, told a reporter for France 24: “This event is a way for us to say loud and proud that Christians are here.”

Speaking to reporters from Agence France-Presse, Sylvie Leclerc, a 51-year-old teacher, also said she and her fellow Christians want to share their fervour for their faith. “You don’t hear much from us Catholics, but now we’re going to make some noise!” she said. “But to proclaim love, peace, joy.”

articles.title: German town bans 'stumbling stone' memorials to Nazi victims
articles.summary: Germany's education minister has branded the ban on the small brass memorial plaques a "scandal".

blocks.text: There has been a wave of criticism in Germany after the town of Heidenau, near Dresden in Saxony, decided to ban "stumbling stone" memorials to victims of the Nazis.
Germany's Education Minister Karin Prien told newspaper Bild that the ban was a "scandal".
Since the 1990s, many towns in countries across Europe, including in Germany and Austria, have embedded small brass plaques in the streets in memory of Jews and other victims of Nazi atrocities.
The plaques, called Stolpersteine in German, are often placed outside the houses where the victims used to live or work. They are frequently funded by donations.
But now councillors from the Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) party and the conservative CDU in Heidenau have voted to ban stumbling stones - or "Stolpersteine" in German - in their town.
The AfD in Saxony has been classified as extreme-right by German intelligence, a designation the party rejects.
The motion in the town council said that many citizens felt that this form of commemoration of Nazi victims was inappropriate.
Memorials should in future be placed at the city's Nordfriedhof cemetery to make it "impossible to step directly onto the memorial elements", the motion stated.
However, Karin Prien, a member of the CDU, criticised the decision.

"Anyone who banishes Stolpersteine and memorial sites commemorating Jewish life from public spaces to the cemetery is prioritising death over life and rendering Jewish people invisible once again," she told Bild.
She said her own CDU party in Saxony also bore responsibility for the decision.
Charlotte Knobloch, a Holocaust survivor and president of the Jewish Community in Munich, said that removing memorials from the cityscape was "completely the wrong approach".
She told the Funke Media Group that she was "appalled that a democratic party would stoop to supporting such a transparent manoeuvre by the extremists of the AfD".

Knobloch said that she was not a supporter of the stumbling stones, but added that "decentralised remembrance – which is not banished from public space but, on the contrary, permeates and shapes it" was crucial to a genuine culture of remembrance.
In her own city of Munich, there are no Stolpersteine on municipal land. Instead, the city allows memorial plaques on public buildings.
As the name suggests, Stolpersteine are intended as memorials people stumble upon, making them reflect on the history of their location.
Gunter Demnig, the artist who initiated the Stolperstein project, said that given the recent electoral successes of the AfD "it was certainly to be expected that something like this would happen".
The AfD recently secured major victories in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.
Some branches of the populist AfD are classed as right-wing extremist by domestic intelligence, a designation the party strongly rejects.
Its anti-immigration, "Germany first" and Russian-friendly agenda has found fertile ground in the country's former communist east.

articles.title: Russia expected to intensify hybrid war on Europe
articles.summary: Drone explosions, airspace violations, arson attacks: Poland, Romania, and Moldova are now regularly targeted in Russian attacks against Ukraine. More governments are calling these attacks deliberate…

image.caption: Aftermath of a drone attack near the Ukrainian-Moldovan border Image: OdeskaODA/Telegram

blocks.text: Just a few months ago, Russia's war was an distant reality for many people in Europe outside of Ukraine. If Russian drones occasionally entered the airspace of countries like Poland or Romania, even official statements seemed strangely dismissive and abstract. Even after a Russian drone struck a high-rise apartment building in the eastern Romanian city of Galati in late May this year, many EU and NATO representatives hesitated to accuse Russia of intentional action. At most, there was discussion of hybrid warfare.

The situation has changed radically since the summer. Drone overflights have become almost daily in certain parts of central and southeastern Europe, and there have even been crashes and explosions, particularly in countries bordering Ukraine. Alerts are becoming more frequent, with authorities increasingly having to close airspace or suspend operations at airports, as unauthorized flights are detected. Russia has been bombing border crossings, infrastructure and trains in Ukraine, but very close to other borders. Acts of sabotage are also increasingly common.
For the Baltic states, Poland, Moldova and Romania in particular, the war has long ceased to be "hybrid." More and more, politicians in these countries are saying that Russia is acting deliberately.
Lessons from Latvia: How to deal with Russian hybrid threats
Drones violate Moldovan and Romanian airspace

This became evident this week in an unprecedented manner. Moldova recorded four drones entering Moldovan airspace, two of which exploded in Moldovan territory. Wreckage of another was also found. The country's northern airspace was closed temporarily. Two drones also violated Romanian airspace; with one crashing near the northern town of Solca. A nearby border crossing with Ukraine a few dozen kilometers away was closed as a result. NATO aircraft were scrambled near the Danube Delta.

blocks.caption: The wreckage of a drone found in Moldova Image: Polizei der Republik Moldau

blocks.text: The scrambling of NATO aircraft has become more common in response to Russian air attacks in Ukraine.

In Poland, NATO fighter jets were scrambled twice in response to Russian attacks near the border with Ukraine. Two Polish border crossings were evacuated after a fire broke out at a Starlink ground station near the village of Wola Krobowska, 40 kilomters (ca. 25 miles) south of the Polish capital Warsaw, on Wednesday night. The station is used to route internet traffic through Poland to Ukraine.
On the same day, a Russian Mi-8 helicopter violated Polish airspace and remained there for 42 seconds according to the Polish military.
Polish Prime Minister Tusk says Europe needs to prepare
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk spoke very bluntly in Krakow on Thursday and said that Russia was refining its "disgusting forms of pressure" and Poland must be prepared for them.

Russian President Vladimir Putin "wants to exhaust Ukraine by destroying its industrial and energy infrastructure, but he also wants to exhaust Europe," Tusk said. He added that there was a suspicion that the fire at the Starlink ground station had been deliberate.
Earlier this month, Tusk had already warned the Polish parliament that there might be Russian drone and even missile attacks against those who supported Ukraine.

blocks.caption: Donald Tusk has warned that Poland has to prepare for possible drone attacks Image: Lukasz Glowala/REUTERS

blocks.text: Moldovan President Maia Sandu also reacted very strongly on Thursday, saying that Russia's war was a danger to all of Europe and reasserting Moldova's support for Ukraine.

In Romania, reactions were less clear. Defense Minister Radu Miruta said that not more than a "diplomatic protest" was needed, though he acknowledged that the drone that had crashed in Solca had new technical features, which suggested it could be a newer type of Russian jet-powered drone.

In New York on Wednesday, in his address to the United Nations General Assembly, Romanian President Nicusor Dan had said: "We are in the fifth year of the illegal, unprovoked and unjustified war of aggression waged on a large scale against Ukraine by a permanent member of the Security Council." He had added that as the "EU member state with the longest border with Ukraine, Romania has directly felt the effects of this war through repeated violations of our airspace."

And he too reasserted support for Ukraine: "We have said it before, and we say it again: Romania will stand with Ukraine and its people, who are acting in legitimate self-defense, for as long as it takes."

blocks.caption: Romanian President Nicusor Dan said Romania would stand by Ukraine Image: Heather Khalifa/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Attacks on western Europe from the Mediterranean?

Meanwhile, there is growing speculation that Russia could expand its war to Western Europe. On Thursday, the Spanish newspaper El Mundo published information about a CIA report warning that Russia could be preparing drone attacks on Italy, France and Spain. The attacks could be launched from international waters in the Mediterranean and from vessels that were part of Russia's shadow fleet.

There has been no official confirmation so far. French President Emmanuel Macron said that that the CIA had not informed France of this information, but he did say that the possibility Russia could launch an attack against Europe was "plausible."

blocks.caption: French President Emmanuel Macron said the CIA had not warned France of possible drone attacks from international waters Image: Ludovic Marin/AFP

blocks.text: At a press conference in Denmark on Thursday, politicians and military officials warned that Russia was expected to intensify its hybrid war against the West and NATO in the coming months. The situation is currently the most serious since the end of the Cold War," said Defense Minister Jeppe Bruus.
This article was originally published in German.

articles.title: Security lapses at Utah campus where Charlie Kirk was killed, review says
articles.summary: The indpendent report also says Kirk's aides insisted he speak outdoors, overriding concerns from campus officials.

blocks.text: An independent review has pointed to a number of security shortcomings at the Utah campus where conservative activist Charlie Kirk was shot dead last year.

The report said Utah Valley University (UVU) did not carry out a proper written security assessment nor prepare an event action plan, deferring key decision-making about the event to Kirk's conservative organisation Turning Point USA.
It also said that Kirk's aides had insisted on a outdoor venue, overriding security concerns from campus officials, who then failed to properly assess the dangers.
The 31-year-old activist had been addressing thousands of people in an Orem campus courtyard when he was shot from a nearby rooftop on 10 September 2025.
Kirk's family said the report reinforced their concerns about how the event was managed.

University officials had raised concerns in August 2025 about holding the event at a location surrounded by tall buildings and had suggested alternative venues, including some indoors, the report, external - published by UVU - says.
"But a Turning Point representative insisted that Kirk speak at a campus courtyard because he had been there previously and the organisation was familiar with the location," it adds.
Despite the "significant protective operations considerations", no line-of-sight assessment was documented in the planning process, the external consultants note.
They also identified shortcomings in the co-ordination between university police and Kirk's private security team.
A proposed meeting between the university's police chief and Turning Point security shortly before the event did not take place, the report said.

The reviewers described the absence of a joint security briefing and walk-through as a missed opportunity to have identified risks, clarified responsibilities and considered additional security measures.
However, the review concluded that no university employee or representative had acted in bad faith or shown "willful and wanton disregard" for anyone's safety.
Kirk's family has previously accused the university of serious security failures and has filed a wrongful-death notice, a step that can precede legal action.
The family's lawyer, Brett Parkinson, said the independent report released on Friday backed up the concerns raised by Kirk's loved ones.

"The buck stopped with UVU leadership and law enforcement," Parkinson said in a statement to the Associated Press. "Justice for Charlie and his family requires true accountability for UVU's fatal shortcomings that day."
When asked for comment on the findings, Turning Point USA referred to Parkinson's statement.
The review makes numerous recommendations aimed at improving security for major campus events.
UVU President Jon Anderson said the university must "learn from the findings of this review, and follow through on its recommendations".

It has previously been reported that the campus police failed to conduct security procedures now common practice at high-profile events, including flying a drone to monitor rooftops or security screening like bag checks and metal detectors.

Kirk had been debating UVU students about US mass shootings, as part of a series of events across different university campuses, when he was shot in the neck shortly after noon. He was rushed to hospital but later pronounced dead.
His alleged killer, Tyler Robinson, has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder in connection with Kirk's death. Prosecutors are seeking the death penalty.

articles.title: Pakistan: Suicide attack at police stop kills at least 11
articles.summary: The blast was claimed by the Pakistani Taliban, which has stepped up attacks on Pakistani security forces in recent years.

image.caption: Islamist militants, led by the TTP, have kept up attacks on police and the army in northwestern Pakistan [FILE: September 18, 2026]Image: Hussain Ali/Anadolu/picture alliance

blocks.text: At least 11 people were killed in a suicide bombing in northwestern Pakistan on Saturday, authorities said.
The blast happened just two days after fighting between Pakistan and Afghanistan along their southwestern border killed at least 13 members of the Afghan Taliban.
Are Pakistan and Afghanistan heading for war?
What do we know?
Police said the bomber detonated an explosives-laden vehicle at a roadside police checkpoint in Dera Ismail Khan, the country's 10th largest city.
Dera Ismail Khan sits in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, which runs along the border with Afghanistan and has been repeatedly hit by Islamist militant violence.
Around 30 others were wounded in the blast, mostly security personnel and passersby, a police official said.
Emergency teams from Rescue 1122 provided medical ​assistance to ‌the wounded and took them to the hospital, the ​service said.
Police said some of the injured were in a critical condition.
The Pakistani Taliban — Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) — an Islamist militant group that targets the Pakistani state, claimed responsibility in a statement.
Islamist attacks on the rise in Pakistan
Pakistan has experienced a surge in militant attacks in recent years.
Many of them have been claimed by the TTP and the outlawed Baloch Liberation Army, or BLA, a separatist group mainly active in neighboring Balochistan province.
The TTP is aligned with Afghanistan's Taliban, which returned to power in Afghanistan in 2021 when US and NATO troops pulled out.
How 5 years of Taliban rule have changed Afghanistan
Pakistan has repeatedly accused Kabul of allowing TTP members to operate from Afghan soil and demanded firmer action to stop cross-border attacks.
The Taliban have denied allowing their territory to be used for attacks.
The rift has sparked cross-border attacks by both countries, with Pakistan carrying out deadly airstrikes it says target militants on Afghan soil.
China, Turkey, Qatar and Saudi Arabia are trying to mediate a lasting peace between the two neighbors.

articles.title: Remulla slams LTO over alleged third-party insurance scheme
articles.summary: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Saturday slammed the Land Transportation Office (LTO) over an alleged scheme involving third-party liability insurance that he said leaves accident victims unable…

blocks.text: Published September 26, 2026 9:53pm

Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Saturday slammed the Land Transportation Office (LTO) over an alleged scheme involving third-party liability insurance that he said leaves accident victims unable to claim benefits.

“The problem is, what we really need to watch out for is the concept of third-party liability insurance. They formed a cartel, which is why the Insurance Commission is having problems,” Remulla said in his radio program.
Remulla alleged that the LTO does not provide a service to help accident victims claim their insurance benefits.
"The problem is, when a person gets into an accident, there is no service or assistance [from the LTO]. They are only concerned with money," he said.

"Especially now, when a motorcycle is hit by a car, shouldn't third-party liability insurance apply? How can they make a claim? Have you ever seen a police officer tell someone, ‘Go ahead and claim insurance for your injury’?" Remulla added.
Remulla also criticized the LTO and the Insurance Commission, accusing both agencies of allegedly being more focused on money than on helping accident victims claim insurance benefits.
“That’s the problem with the LTO; it’s all about money. That’s wrong. The Insurance Commission is also all about money, ” he said.
Emissions testing
Remulla also slammed the LTO over an alleged “non-appearance” scheme involving Private Motor Vehicle Inspection Centers (PMVICs), which he said contributes to air pollution in the country.
“The emissions testing is not actually being conducted. It’s a non-appearance arrangement,” he said.
“At least have them tested after five years or after 10 years. All of them should be tested,” he added.
Remulla said some emission testing centers are reporting as many as 5,000 emission tests a month, although the actual number of vehicles undergoing testing is lower.
GMA News Online has sought the LTO’s comment on Remulla’s allegations.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Canadian citizen detained at U.S. border crossing, questioned about voting for hours

image.caption: Paige Adamson says she was detained until nearly 3 a.m. PT and was 'basically treated like a criminal' when she attempted to cross the Canada-U.S. border at the Point Roberts border crossing on Sept. 15. (Ben Nelms/CBC)

blocks.text: British Columbia

Paige Adamson was on her way home from a birthday dinner in Tsawwassen, B.C., on Sept. 15 when she was stopped at the Point Roberts border crossing and questioned about voting for hours. Lawyers are raising concerns around vulnerabilities Canadians face while living in the U.S., especially over being registered to vote.
'Tip of the iceberg': One lawyer warns more Canadians could be detained over illegal voting concerns
Paige Adamson was on her way home from a birthday dinner in Tsawwassen, B.C., on Sept. 15 when she was stopped at the Point Roberts border crossing.
It was a regular stop that Adamson — a Canadian citizen who has lived in Point Roberts, Wash., as a U.S. permanent resident for 14 years — had grown used to.
But this time, they had a new question for her.
"The very first thing she asked was, 'Have you ever voted in a federal U.S. election?'" said Adamson.
Adamson, 61, said she told the border agent she had never voted in a federal election.
"They immediately said, 'Park over here and come into the office.'"

What happened next, Adamson said, was a nearly six-hour-long process — where she went through secondary inspection just after 9 p.m., was interrogated until after 2 a.m. and signed documents before being admitted into the U.S.
One of the documents CBC News reviewed said Adamson "must surrender for removal from the United States, if so ordered."

Lawyers who spoke with CBC News said U.S. voter registration systems can sometimes catch non-citizens up in errors, and one of them says he has seen an uptick in non-citizens being questioned in the last week.
Grounds for removal

According to documents provided by Adamson, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) alleges she falsely claimed she was a U.S. citizen "for the purposes of registering to vote in Whatcom County, Washington state."
The department also alleges Adamson voted in Washington state's 2018 general election.
DHS cites those allegations as grounds for removing Adamson from the U.S.

But Adamson maintained during questioning, a transcript reviewed by CBC News showed, that she has never voted in a federal election and doesn't remember ever voting in a state election — though she acknowledged receiving a ballot and may have been registered.
Adamson is now scheduled to appear for a hearing in Seattle, and is grappling with potentially being removed from the state she has lived in since 2012.
"My anxiety is over the top," she said.
A broader trend
In the past week and a half, immigration lawyer Len Saunders said he has received calls from three people — including Adamson — about being detained at the border and questioned about voting.
One, he said, was a Blaine, Wash., resident who crosses the border daily to work as a nurse in B.C.
Saunders said three near-identical situations like this in such a short period is unprecedented in his career that stretches back more than 25 years.
The Blaine-based lawyer told CBC News there could be hundreds of Canadians facing similar issues, and expects more cases as Canadians cross the border during the holidays.
"This is just the tip of the iceberg," he said.
B.C. immigration lawyer Chris Anders said border enforcement is "way, way stricter and tougher" than at any point in the last two decades.
He said the databases used by border officials are constantly expanding, meaning something that did not cause problems for someone previously could suddenly pop up during a new entry.
Voter registration issues
Washington state automatically registers some eligible voters when they get or renew a driver's licence or state ID, but the state says the system is tied to proof of U.S. citizenship.

But internal Washington Department of Licensing emails, obtained by the non-profit Federation for American Immigration Reform through a Freedom of Information request, show instances where non-citizens were registered to vote.
"A lot of Canadians say, 'Well, I thought I was entitled to [vote] because I went in, got my driver's licence and they registered me to vote,'" said Saunders.

items: Change in Canada's citizenship law hitting U.S. archives
Winnipeg-born man deported back to Canada after 9 months in ICE detention

blocks.text: Saunders said that in those situations, he has told clients to immediately deregister and submit a declaration saying they "unknowingly registered or unknowingly voted," and that used to be a consistent solution.
"Now, it seems to be a completely different scenario during this current administration."
The detainment

In an email to CBC News, a spokesperson for the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) said when a permanent resident arrives at a port of entry, officers screen their documentation against federal and state databases.

The CBP says if those records indicate "potential unlawful voter registration, illegal voting, or a previous false claim to U.S. citizenship," the individual is subject to "rigorous examination and detailed questioning."
Depending on the case, an individual may face "prolonged" immigration inspections, receive a notice to appear and formal removal proceedings, the spokesperson said.
Are U.S. border agents allowed to search my phone? Your border questions answered
Adamson said she wasn't offered water until around the five-hour mark of her detainment, and no one asked whether she needed to use the bathroom.
"I was basically treated like a criminal," she said.
She said the large Canadian population in Point Roberts — an exclave of the U.S. located just south of Delta, B.C. — has left her concerned that some of her neighbours could face similar problems.
"This beautiful little place, it's kind of being invaded," she said.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Arden McLeod, from Vancouver, is an associate producer with CBC News. He has a passion for community storytelling, local news, and reflecting the values of B.C. He graduated from the British Columbia Institute of Technology's broadcast and online journalism program. You can reach him at Arden.McLeod@cbc.ca.

articles.title: B.C. man uses motion-activated zombie to scare bears away from garbage
articles.summary: More than 33 bears have been killed by conservation officers in B.C. this year, including two that entered stores through automatic sliding doors in Hope and Squamish. It's led to creative solutions…

image.caption: Stephen Fryer's surveillance footage captured a bear being scared off by the motion-activated Halloween decoration, a creative solution being employed to scare the animals away as they seek food at lower elevations. (Submitted by Stephen Fryer)

blocks.text: British Columbia

More than 33 bears have been killed by conservation officers in B.C. this year, including two that entered stores through automatic sliding doors in Hope and Squamish. It's led to creative solutions to keep the hungry animals away from attractants.
The bears have been ripping off Stephen Fryer's bins, destroying the handles and lids
A Squamish, B.C., homeowner is using a motion-activated Halloween decoration to scare bears away from his garbage bins.
Stephen Fryer has been dealing with bears constantly in the Brackendale neighbourhood, about 50 kilometres north of Vancouver.
"They're around us every single day," Fryer said.

Officials say animals are looking for food at lower elevations, after drought and wildfires at higher elevations have reduced their food sources. Fryer is one homeowner who is trying a creative way to keep the bears out of his garbage.
He stores his bins outside, as he does not have a garage, and the bears often tip the bins to get inside.
"The garbage, the handles have been like chewed off — not ripped off, chewed off, because they're trying to get into it," Fryer said.
Fryer decided to reinforce the bins to the side of his house with a bolt and strap — but that didn't work either.
"One of them finally figured out how to rip it out of the wall and pulled the ... I-hook out of the wall and off the strap," Fryer said.
His wife had asked for the Halloween decorations to be set up in September, and that's when Fryer got an idea to put a motion-activated zombie on top of the garbage bins.
"It absolutely scared the bear to the point where it it peed itself," Fryer said.
Squamish man uses Halloween decorations to keep bears out of garbage
Surveillance video shows a burly black bear sniffing the bins. Moments later, the zombie lets out a scream and pops up.
"Another one came by, and it went off," Fryer said.

items: Bear killed by authorities after wandering through pharmacy with cub in Hope

blocks.text: Since the zombie was installed, the bears have been deterred.
"As funny as that is, it's totally worked," Fryer said.
More than 30 bears killed
In Squamish, 90 tickets have been issued in connection with the wildlife attractant bylaw, which includes leaving garbage out and not picking up fruit from fallen trees.
"The number of complaints we're getting is pretty high each day," said Sgt. Chris Doyle with the BCCOS's Sea-to-Sky zone.
The BCCOS said more bears are being seen at lower elevations.
"There's a lot less berries at higher elevations than there should be for a normal year, and that's likely driving a lot of the conflict," Doyle said.
Between January and July this year, conservation officers have responded to 13,672 calls regarding black bears in B.C.
At least 33 black bears have been killed in the first seven months of the year. September is often the deadliest month, with nine being killed last year.
Bears killed after entering stores
A bear wandered into a Squamish grocery store on Sept. 17 around 3 p.m. PT through automatic sliding doors.
Video captured the bear walking near the produce section of the store, and shortly after, it left through the sliding doors.
The B.C. Conservation Officer Service (BCCOS) said the bear also entered another business in the downtown area.
When officers arrived, the bear was outside the store. Officers tranquillized the bear and killed it.
In a statement, the service said the bear was killed "due to public safety concerns".
A similar incident occurred in Hope recently when a black bear and its cub entered a pharmacy on Sept. 20 through automatic sliding doors.
BCCOS confirmed the mother bear was killed and the cub was released into a wilderness area.

"Bears that pose a serious threat to public safety, such as those that display a minimal fear of people or are conditioned to non-natural food sources, are not candidates for relocation or rehabilitation, as the risk is simply far too great," said the service.
Calls for change
Advocates argue that more can be done to prevent bears from being killed.
Holly Reisner with North Shore Black Bear Society said there has been an increased level of bear activity in B.C.
"These automated doors are just allowing bears to enter," Reisner said. "The bears are very attracted by any type of odour."
She's encouraging businesses to consider replacing the doors so bears cannot enter.
Lesley Fox, executive director of The Fur-Bearers, said a bear walking through a doorway should not be a death sentence.
"The question should be what the bear actually did, whether they posed a genuine threat, and whether reasonable non-lethal options were available," Fox said.

items: 'He could barely paddle anymore': B.C. family rescues bear cub from Okanagan Lake

blocks.text: She suggests better security features be installed.
"These are preventable problems," Fox said.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Alanna Kelly is a CBC News journalist based in Squamish, B.C., covering the Sea-to-Sky region, including Whistler, Pemberton and the Sunshine Coast. You can email story ideas to alanna.kelly@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Huge crowds greet Pope in Paris ahead of open-air Mass
articles.summary: More than half a million people are expected to attend the event in the heart of the French capital.

blocks.text: Image source, Reuters
Hundreds of thousands of people have greeted Pope Leo XIV in the centre of Paris ahead of a giant open-air Mass.
Crowds cheered as the pontiff moved down the Champs-Élysées Avenue beneath the Arc de Triomphe, waving to crowds from his popemobile.
The head of the Catholic Church blessed several babies as he stopped at different stages along the avenue as chants of "Leo, Leo" rang out.
More than half a million people are expected to attend the event in the heart of the French capital on Saturday and a special altar has been built on the Place de la Concorde for the ceremony.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Thousands have gathered along Champs-Elysees Avenue ahead of Pope Leo's open-air Mass

blocks.text: Thousands have gathered along Champs-Elysees Avenue ahead of Pope Leo's open-air Mass

French President Emmanuel Macron, who met Leo for an hour of talks on Friday, will not be at any of the Pope's Masses during his four-day visit to France, largely to avoid breaching France's strict separation of state and religion.
But the Champs-Élysées Mass will be attended by Macron's wife Brigitte and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu.
Several candidates for next year's presidential election are also expected to attend.

Marine Le Pen of the hard-right National Rally party and conservative Bruno Retailleau were both pictured at the Place de la Concorde ahead of the event, while centrists Edouard Philippe and Gabriel Attal are also due to be there.
Mayor of Le Havre and former French Prime Minister Edouard Philippe and former Prime Minister Francois Fillon were both also seen at the Place de la Concorde.

blocks.caption: The pope moves through crowds in his popemobile. Several police officers can be seen nearby. Members of the crowd can be seen waving flags.

blocks.text: Earlier on Saturday, the Pope met migrants as he visited the Maison Bakhita centre, an association supporting refugees, and praised the organisation for inviting "us to see those who are invisible".
During the visit Leo said it was "possible to encounter one another and to live together in dignity and peace".
He also stressed the "the fundamental role of women in building a civilisation of love".
The Pope also issued a warning about the dangers of artificial intelligence (AI) at the start of his visit to France on Friday.
Leo cautioned against "losing our humanity amid a paradise of machines" in wide-ranging remarks to Church and state officials at the Élysée Palace.
Why is the Pope in France?

blocks.caption: A cardboard cut out of Pope Leo is seen above the crowds at the Place de la Concorde

blocks.text: Large crowds are expected throughout the pontiff's trip, which the Church believes reflects a growing spirituality among the French and other Europeans.
On Sunday, 150,000 have signed up to attend mass in the Pyrenean sanctuary of Lourdes.

The Pope will be in Metz, in northeast France, on Monday where he will pay tribute to Robert Schuman (1886-1963), a founding father of the European Union and a fervent Catholic who is today a candidate for beatification.
Born in Chicago in 1955, Pope Leo XIV was originally called Robert Prevost – a French name.

His paternal grandmother was born in Le Havre in Normandy in 1894. When she married in the US many years later, she and her Italian husband took the name Prevost, which had been her mother's maiden name.

articles.title: German Olympic Committee names Munich as bid city choice
articles.summary: Munich has been voted as the city that will bid for the Olympics in 2036, 2040 or 2044. Berlin had been in the running but withdrew on Thursday.

image.caption: Germany's entry will have to compete against other international cities to host the OlympicsImage: Franz Feiner/Eibner-Presse/picture alliance

blocks.text: The German Olympic Sports Confederation (DOSB) on Saturday announced it chose Munich as Germany's entry to bid for at least the next three Olympic Summer Games.

Ahead of the vote, former Olympic champion and new Sports Minister Ronald Rauhe said: "We have an international task to fulfill and must enter the race with the city or region that gives Germany the greatest chances internationally. The decision on that is made by sport, and I assume that it will make it with a great deal of responsibility."
Berlin bowing out created two-horse race
Munich and a Cologne-led bid by the Rhine-Ruhr region were the only two in contention.
As many as 17.6 million tickets could be sold for the Games in Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr, more than ever before at a Games, the premier of North Rhine-Westphalia said recently.
Munich was campaigning after two failed bids for the 2018 and 2022 Winter Games and having previously hosted the 1972 Summer Olympics.
Up until Thursday, Berlin had been among the cities in contention, but the city's mayor announced that the city would withdraw from the race.

The withdrawal comes after the socialist Left Party's victory in the German capital's elections last weekend. The party's lead candidate and potential mayor, Elif Eralp, said she did not support Berlin's bid.
Take a tour of Berlin's iconic Olympic Stadium
Sports minister has sights set on 2040
On Friday, Sports Minister Ronald Rauhe said he would welcome a German Olympic bid for the 2040 Games, with it coinciding with an important historical milestone.

blocks.caption: Sports Minister Ronald Rauhe said the city or region that gave Germany the greatest chances internationally should be voted forImage: dts-Agentur/picture alliance

blocks.text: "2040 will mark the 50th anniversary of reunification. Here we could send a great signal that also aligns with the values of the Olympic Games,” Rauhe told German news agency dpa ahead of the deciding vote on Saturday.

"Based on my personal history, 2040 would be my favorite date. That has to do with the fact that I'm a Berlin child. As a schoolchild, I experienced what happens to people when a wall falls, when people grow together again, when two population groups that had been separated become a community again,” Rauhe said.
"Ultimately, though, one thing matters above all: bringing the Olympic and Paralympic Games back to our country. No matter when," Rauhe said.
